sub -dŭbĭto , āre, v. n.,
I.to be a little doubtful or undecided, to have some hesitation (Ciceron.): “antea subdubitabam,” Cic. Att. 14, 15, 2 : “significabant tuae litterae, te subdubitare, quā essem erga illum voluntate,” id. Fam. 2, 13, 2 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
